nodes.text: Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}$ be a set containing no solutions to $a+b=c$. Must there be a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}\backslash S$ of cardinality continuum such that $A+A\subseteq \mathbb{R}\backslash S$?

#949 : [Er77c] ramsey theory Erdős suggests that if the answer is no one could consider the variant where we assume that $S$ is Sidon (i.e. all $a+b$ with $a,b\in S$ are distinct, aside from the trivial coincidences). In the comments Dillies gives a positive proof of this, found by AlphaProof: in other words, if $S\subset \mathbb{R}$ is a Sidon set then there exists $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}\backslash S$ of cardinality continuum such that $A+A\subseteq \mathbb{R}\backslash S$.
